newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates firm for VLCCs Mideast/east VLC.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates firm for VLCCs Mideast/east VLC.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates for 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) were firmer on Wednesday for Mideast/East routes after good recent chartering of vessels, shipbrokers said.
Brokers said the rate was now W67.5-W70 for VLCCs sailing from the Mideast to Japan, compared to around W65 last week.

They saw the evidence in Tonen's fixture for a Mideast/Japan voyage of the 250,000 tonne Suzuka at W67.5, Cosmo's fixture of the Samco Europe at W68.5 and Texaco's charter of the World Prince for a Mideast/East voyage at W73.5.

"A lot of people got caught out for the first half of the month," one broker said. "I am not sure if they are going to stay up here because a lot of vessels have been going to the Red Sea recently and it remains to be seen if they are going to get stuck there waiting in demurrage or not."

Rates for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes plying UK/Cont routes were slightly easier again from recent sky-high levels, with two fresh fixtures seen for May at W137.5, compared with prices as high as W155 last week.
Fuel oil tankers of 25,000 tonnes travelling within northwestern Europe continued to rise steadily.
Brokers said they expected a repeat of the last couple of years when rates rose from around W165 in previous winters to W270 last year and W300 the year before.
IPCO was heard to have fixed the Dubulti in May for W220, and this rate was expected to rise.
"We have seen a steady increase in the last two weeks... I cannot imagine rates are going to drop from here," one broker said.
